releases.name: v1.0.0 — First public release
releases.body:
First public release, published to npm as `opencode-provider-quota`.

## Install

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["opencode-provider-quota@1.0.0"]
}
```

OpenCode installs this automatically via Bun at startup. No manual download, no digest pinning, no chezmoi script — that whole file-path/GitHub-release deployment model from earlier private-repo releases is retired in favor of native npm distribution.

## What changed from earlier private iterations

- Dropped the Anthropic/Claude adapter entirely. It was gated off by default already; removing it avoids publishing code that queries an unofficial endpoint OpenCode's own docs flag as a policy concern for Claude Pro/Max subscriptions.
- Renamed the package (the original working name, `opencode-quota-sidebar`, was already taken by an unrelated project).
- Repo made public after a full-history secrets scan (12 commits, all blobs) found nothing sensitive.

## What it does

Reads OpenAI and GitHub Copilot subscription quota from OpenCode's local OAuth credentials and renders it as a bar in the sidebar. Fixed HTTPS endpoints only, no repository-local config, no telemetry, no credential persistence — see SECURITY.md.

10 parser tests and a real-OpenTUI-renderer UI test cover both providers, including OpenAI's business-plan credit-budget quota shape.

releases.name: v0.2.2 — Sidebar cleanup
releases.body:
Three sidebar behavior changes, no security or deployment changes.

- Claude's card is no longer rendered while its unofficial endpoint is disabled (the default). Previously it showed a permanent disabled: unofficial endpoint line; the provider is now skipped entirely and never queried.
- The absolute OpenAI credit balance (e.g. 5,390 of 7,500 credits left) is no longer rendered. The bar and reset time remain; the parsing that computes the balance is unchanged and still tested.
- Removed the unrelated opencode-token-usage plugin from the managed OpenCode configuration. It is a separate project by a different author and was not part of this plugin.

releases.name: v0.2.1 — Minimal verifiable deployment
releases.body:
Changes how the plugin is deployed, with no behaviour change to the sidebar.

The release now ships a minimal artifact containing only package.json and dist, about 8 KB. OpenCode embeds @opentui/core, @opentui/solid and solid-js in its own binary and provides them to plugins, so those are now declared as optional peer dependencies instead of vendored runtime dependencies. The deployed plugin needs no node_modules, which removes roughly 135 MB and 129 packages from the install, along with their advisories. No package manager or compiler runs on the target machine.

The archive is published with a SHA-256 digest so the chezmoi install script can verify it before extracting, and installs atomically.

releases.name: v0.2.0 — OpenAI quota bar
releases.body: Exposes the OpenAI quota bar. The account uses a business plan, where OpenAI leaves the consumer rate-limit windows null and reports a credit budget under spend_control.individual_limit instead. That budget now drives the bar, with the absolute balance shown beneath it, for example 5,390 of 7,500 credits left. Consumer 5h and weekly windows are still read when present. Fixes two parsing bugs found while investigating: OpenAI reset timestamps are epoch seconds and were previously interpreted as milliseconds, producing 1976 dates; and the percent heuristic rescaled values at or below 1, which would have displayed a 1% remainder as 100%. Percentages are now read on a documented 0-100 scale, and ratios are converted explicitly. Adds invalidateQuotaCache for forced refresh and test isolation. Thirteen tests pass, including a rendered business-plan sidebar frame.

releases.name: v0.1.5 — Retry after sleep
releases.body: Retries transient provider failures five seconds after an interrupted request instead of caching aborted snapshots. Interrupted fetches now show request interrupted; retrying while the sidebar recovers. Uses a monochrome bar presentation: white provider bars, black percentage labels, no Copilot Premium label, and a single quota bar beside a provider name when it has only one window. Eight parser tests and the built UI regression test pass.
